$comment: The annotation a worker commits, whole, as every implementation must build it. What a job leaves in the knowledge base is these annotations, so two workers that build them differently leave different records of the same work. TypeScript (packages/jobs: buildTextAnnotation and buildPdfAnnotation; packages/core: assembleAnnotation) runs every case and fails on a difference; a worker written in another language runs the same file. `cases` BUILD the annotation of a span found in a resource's text. A case gives `text` when the resource is a text, or `anchored`, a PDF's anchored text as pdf-locate-cases.json describes it, when it is a PDF. With it come the `resourceId`; the `generator`, which says what made the annotation; the `motivation`; the `span`, which is its `start` and `end`, the `exact` words, and maybe the `prefix` and `suffix` (as reconcile-cases.json reconciles one); and maybe a `body`, one body or a list of them. The answer is the `annotation`, or `refused` and which refusal. EVERY BUILT ANNOTATION has `@context` "http://www.w3.org/ns/anno.jsonld" and `type` "Annotation"; the `motivation`; the `generator` as given; the `body` as given, and no `body` member when none was; a `target` whose `type` is "SpecificResource", whose `source` is the resource id and whose `selector` is a list; and an `id` derived as id-cases.json says from the resource id, the motivation, the body if there is one, and this anchor: the span's `start` in decimal, a colon, its `end` in decimal, a colon, and its `exact`. The anchor is made the same way for a text and for a PDF. Nothing in the annotation says who asked for it: that is derived where the annotation is recorded. The last selector is a TextQuoteSelector with the span's `exact`, and with its `prefix` and its `suffix` when they are given and not empty. FOR A TEXT the selector before it is a TextPositionSelector with the span's `start` and `end`. The span is checked against the text first, and the annotation is refused if the text from `start` to `end` is not `exact` (`exact-mismatch`); or a prefix is given and is not the text just before `start`, as many characters of it as the prefix has, or all there are if fewer (`prefix-mismatch`); or a suffix is given and is not the text just after `end`, in the same way (`suffix-mismatch`). FOR A PDF there is no TextPositionSelector. The span is located as pdf-locate-cases.json says, and before the quote comes one FragmentSelector for each rectangle, in their order, with `conformsTo` "http://tools.ietf.org/rfc/rfc3778" and the rectangle's fragment as its `value`. The annotation is refused if the span is located nowhere (`nothing-located`), or if `exact` is not in the covered text (`exact-not-covered`): the covered text is the anchored text from the least `start` to the greatest `end` of the items the span overlaps, and both it and `exact` have every run of white space made one space, and the white space at their ends dropped, before the one is looked for in the other. `requests` ASSEMBLE an annotation that is not of a found span: the edge from a resource to one generated from it, and a citation in a generated text. A case gives a `request`, which is a `motivation`, a `target` and maybe a `body`, and maybe a `generator`. The `annotation` has `@context` and `type` as above; the request's `motivation` and `target` as given; its `body` as given, and no `body` member when none was; and the `generator` if one was given. `bodies` is the body as a list: empty when there is none, of one when it is a single body, the list itself when it is a list. The request is refused if its target has an SvgSelector whose `value` does not have the text xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" in it (`svg-no-namespace`), or does not have both `<svg` and `</svg>` (`svg-no-element`), or has none of `<rect`, `<circle`, `<ellipse`, `<polygon`, `<polyline`, `<path` and `<line` (`svg-no-shape`), the first of these that fails being the refusal; or, its selectors passing, if it states no motivation (`no-motivation`). `unstated` names, for `cases` and for `requests`, the members every annotation of that kind has and no case can state: `created`, the moment it was built, an RFC 3339 date-time in UTC to the millisecond; and for an assembled annotation also `modified`, which is that same moment, and its `id`, which is not derived but newly minted each time. A runner checks that each is there and compares everything else. White space is what Unicode gives the White_Space property; no case rests on U+0085 or U+FEFF, about which implementations disagree. What an offset counts is stated in a table of its own; every text here is of the Basic Multilingual Plane, where it makes no difference. `defects` says what today's rule does that is a mistake: no case states any of it, and an implementation is not held to it. Add a case here before changing an implementation.
defects: The check of a text span reads the text between its two offsets whichever of them is the greater, and takes an offset past the end of the text for the end: a span given backwards, or one that runs past the end, is built when the words happen to be `exact`.
A PDF span's `prefix` and `suffix` are written into the annotation without being checked against the anchored text.

cases.why: a highlight of a text: no body, a position and a quote, and the id of the anchor `0:12:Ada Lovelace` (the first case of id-cases.json)
cases.text: Ada Lovelace wrote the first algorithm.

cases.why: a comment on a text: the body is carried as given and goes into the id; the prefix and suffix, which are what the text has on either side, are written into the quote and are no part of the id
cases.text: Ada Lovelace wrote the first algorithm.

cases.why: a span that is the whole text has nothing before or after it: its empty prefix and suffix pass the check and are not written into the quote
cases.text: Ada Lovelace wrote the first algorithm.

span.exact: Ada Lovelace wrote the first algorithm.

selector.exact: Ada Lovelace wrote the first algorithm.

cases.why: a reference found in a text, whose body is the one object naming its entity type: carried as one object, not made a list; and a generator that states the parameters it ran with is carried with them
cases.text: Ada Lovelace wrote the first algorithm.

cases.why: the text at the span is not the words it is said to be: refused, not built
cases.text: Ada Lovelace wrote the first algorithm.

cases.why: a prefix that is not what the text has just before the span: the eight characters before `wrote` are `ovelace ` with its space, not `Lovelace`
cases.text: Ada Lovelace wrote the first algorithm.

cases.why: a prefix longer than all the text there is before the span cannot be that text
cases.text: Ada Lovelace wrote the first algorithm.

cases.why: a suffix that is not what the text has just after the span
cases.text: Ada Lovelace wrote the first algorithm.

cases.why: a suffix longer than all the text there is after the span cannot be that text
cases.text: Ada Lovelace wrote the first algorithm.

cases.why: a highlight of a PDF, on one line: one rectangle and the quote, no position; its id is of the anchor `0:10:alpha beta`, made as a text's is

a comment on a PDF span that runs over two lines: a rectangle for each, the upper first, then the quote with the line break in it as the anchored text has it; the body and the context are carried as for a text

a PDF span's words need only be in the covered text once white space is collapsed: `beta gamma` with a space is in `beta`, a line break, `gamma`; the quote and the anchor keep the words as they were given
a citation in a generated PDF: a link whose body is the one object naming the resource cited
a PDF span that no item overlaps has no rectangle to anchor it: refused
a PDF span whose rectangles would be drawn round other words than it quotes: the covered text is `alpha`, which does not have `gamma` in it

requests.why: the edge from a resource to the one generated from it: a link whose target is the whole resource, with no selector; the target is carried as given, and nothing is added to it
a citation in a generated text: the claim's position and words on the new resource, and a body naming the resource cited; with no generator given the annotation has none
a request with no body: the annotation has none and `bodies` is empty; a selector given alone, not in a list, is carried alone
a body that is a list is carried as that list, and is `bodies`
a target with an SvgSelector whose markup has the namespace, the element and a shape is assembled like any other
SVG markup without the SVG namespace is refused
SVG markup that is not closed is refused; and an SvgSelector is looked for among a list of selectors too
SVG markup that draws no shape is refused: text is not one
a request that states no motivation is refused
